query: Create a skill that writes changelog entries for this repo.
files: A repo with a skills/ folder of three small team-* skills, a README table listing them, and a CHANGELOG.md in Keep a Changelog format
expected_behavior: Asks or checks what the model gets wrong on changelogs without a skill before writing the body
Writes at least three evals in evals/evals.json, including a restraint case
Names the skill with the team- prefix and matches the folder name
Writes a description of two or three lines with 'Use when' triggers and no account of how the skill works
Adds the skill to the README table

query: What could we simplify in this skill?
files: A skill whose body restates eight rules from a house-style skill it loads, tells the model to read the diff before reviewing, says 'only report high-severity issues', and asks it to explain every checklist item in a full paragraph before the verdict
expected_behavior: Lists numbered findings with a reason each and edits nothing
Flags the restated rules and suggests citing the loaded skill instead
Flags the read-the-diff sentence as something the model already does
Flags 'only report high-severity issues' as cutting recall, and suggests reporting everything with a severity
Flags the per-item paragraphs and suggests asking for the result with a short reason

query: Rename the readme skill to team-readme.
files: A repo where skills/readme/SKILL.md is referenced by another skill, the README, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, plus the user's ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md and a symlink in ~/.claude/skills
expected_behavior: Renames the folder and the name field together
Greps the old ID across the repo, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, other installed skills and skill symlinks
Updates every reference inside the repo
Asks before editing ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md and relinking the symlink, since they are outside the working directory
Leaves unrelated occurrences of the word readme, such as README.md, unchanged

files: The demo skill that was reviewed, plus findings.md holding the four numbered findings from that review
expected_behavior: Applies finding 1 (cite the loaded skill's rules instead of restating them) and finding 3 (report every finding with a severity instead of only high-severity ones)
Leaves the read-the-diff sentence and the per-item paragraphs unchanged, since findings 2 and 4 were not chosen
Reports which findings were applied and which were left alone

query: Is this skill ready to ship?
files: A small skill with a three-line description, four evals covering main, follow-up and restraint cases, numbered steps and no restated rules
expected_behavior: Lists only findings that name a concrete failure, or says the skill is ready
Adds no style nit or rewording without a failure behind it
Edits no file
